result.topic_en: Spherical trigonometry notes relating the half-perimeter of a spherical triangle to the radii of its inscribed and escribed circles, together with sine relations involving a triangle's sides, angles and the trihedral (solid) angle at the centre of the sphere.
result.transcription:
Riemann 27
$a+b+c=2s$
$\sin(s-a) = \cot\frac{A}{2}\,\mathrm{tg}\,\varrho$
$\sin s = \cot\frac{B}{2}\,\mathrm{tg}\,\varrho_b$
$\sin(s-c) = \mathrm{tg}\frac{A}{2}\,\mathrm{tg}\,\varrho_b$
$\sin(s-a) = \mathrm{tg}\frac{C}{2}\,\mathrm{tg}\,\varrho_b$

[figure: spherical triangle $ABC$ with inscribed and escribed circle, radius $\varrho_b$]
[figure: small triangle $A$, $B$, $C$] $\sin b$

$OOA = OC\cdot OA\cdot\frac{\sin b}{2}$
$P = OB\cdot OC\cdot OA\cdot\frac{\sin b}{B}\sin\beta$

[figure: triangle $C$, $B$, $A$ with altitude $\beta$]
$\sin\beta\,\sin b$
$\sin\beta = \sin C\,\sin A$
$\sin b\,\sin C\,\sin A = \sin a\,\sin c\,\sin B = \sin c\,\sin b\,\sin a$[?]
$\frac{\sin A}{\sin a} \sim$
